title: Official Zelda Website Raises Eyebrows By Labeling 3DS Game As Playable On Switch
text: Nintendo is celebrating The Legend of Zelda's 40th anniversary in many different ways, but one detail on the company's official website raised confusion--and curiosity-- about a classic 3DS Zelda game. A "History" page on Nintendo's website lists every mainline Zelda game in release order, including the release date and which platforms you can play for each entry. The site marks every game that's playable for Nintendo Switch Online subscribers--and the 2013 3DS game The Legend of Zelda: A Link Between Worlds was marked as such. The NSO icon has since been removed from the site. Currently, the Nintendo Classics library allows NSO subscribers to play select NES, SNES, and Game Boy games, while the Expansion Pack subscription includes access to Nintendo 64, Game Boy Advance, GameCube, and Virtual Boy games. There's currently no way to play 3DS games on Nintendo Switch, prompting the question of whether this was an error on Nintendo's website or an accidental leak that A Link Between Worlds will somehow be playable on Switch. GameSpot has reached out to Nintendo for clarification on the matter. Nintendo's official website briefly listed A Link Between Worlds as a playable game through NSO. The site appropriately labels the Zelda games featured on Nintendo Classics if they are only playable with the Nintendo Switch Online Expansion Pack subscription, which applies to Ocarina of Time ( the original ), Majora's Mask, A Link to the Past/Four Swords on GBA, The Wind Waker, and The Minish Cap. If this labeling for A Link Between Worlds were true, it would be surprising if the Expansion Pack were not required to play it. Nintendo Classics also lacks any Wii or DS games, so jumping straight to 3DS would be a bizarre move for the service. Whatever the case, A Link Between Worlds is a magnificent entry in the Zelda series that deserves to be experienced. GameSpot's 9/10 review of the game called it an "absolute treat to play" with some of the "best Zelda dungeons in years."

title: GTA 6 And These Other Games Can Justify An $80 Price, Expert Says
text: Rockstar's Grand Theft Auto 6 finally releases on November 19, and you'll have to pay at least $80 for it. That's a full $20 more than what GTA 5 cost in 2013 and $10 more than many other big AAA games today. Is $80 going to become the "new normal" for AAA games, or is it, along with Nintendo's Mario Kart World and Tears of the Kingdom for Switch 2 , an outlier at $80? According to Alinea Analytics researcher Rhys Elliott , $80 won't be an across-the-board new price for all games. Some developers will purposefully price their games lower to draw in more consumers--he pointed to games like Expedition 33 ($50), Phantom Blade Zero ($60), and Oblivion Remastered ($50) as examples. A scene from GTA 6. Elliott said that when GTA 6 inevitably becomes a huge success with its $80 and $100 editions, some publishers will be "jumping for joy" because they'll take this as a signal that the market will indeed accept these higher prices. However, Elliott said he hopes the industry doesn't learn the wrong lessons from GTA 6 and its $80 price point. "GTA 6 is as inelastic as things get in entertainment. People will pay anything to get their mitts on this one, which makes it seem like the perfect Trojan horse for an industry-wide price rise," he said. "The $80 price point will be a Godsend to some publishers, but it’ll be a snowball's chance in hell for others. After all, this kind of stuff can be zero-sum. When a player spends $100 on GTA 6, their remaining budget shrinks," he added. Elliott went on to list off some of the studios and game franchises that could likely get their fanbases to buy in at $80. He said these include the next big God of War game after Laufey, the next Naughty Dog game, Intergalactic: The Heretic Prophet, and future Forza titles (assuming Xbox strips them out of Game Pass). Additionally, Elliott said From Software "has the cache" to charge $80 for its new games, while Hogwarts Legacy 2 could also up the price to $80. Elliott added that some of the top sports games could charge more, but that might be a tougher sell considering those games are full of microtransactions already. "So not all games were created equal, and mid-tier AAA publishers--and also bigger publishers offering smaller games or remakes--will price downward at $40-$60," Elliott said. There are a lot of factors at play here. For starters, GTA 5 launched at $60 back in 2013, and that same $60 is worth $86 today after inflation, making GTA 6--at least its $80 edition--effectively cheaper than GTA 5 . At the same time, many people are acutely aware that their pay has not kept up with inflation, while the federal minimum wage hasn't moved up since 2009. GTA 6 is also coming out at a rough time for many people, with gas and grocery prices surging , and the cost of everyday goods generally spiking due in part to increasing inflation. And anyone heading to a store to buy a console to play GTA 6 on is in for some serious sticker shock, as game consoles today are more expensive than ever due to the AI craze. New video games generally staying the same price over the years has had serious negative effects on the entire industry, experts have said. It's part of the reason why publishers now try to squeeze people more with DLC, battle passes, microtransactions, collector's editions, paid early access, and more. Recently, an Xbox advertising chief said price increases would be a hard sell, so the company is turning to ads to help offset ballooning budgets and keep the business healthy.

title: The PS5’s New Graphics-Upscaling Trick Is Spreading To More Games
text: Sony has announced that several more games are getting a Quick Spectral Super Resolution (QSSR) upgrade on PS5. Introduced in September, QSSR is an AI-guided upscaling technology similar to the PS5 Pro's PlayStation Spectral Super Resolution (PSSR), and it originally supported only Marvel's Wolverine and Ghost of Yotei. That lineup is expanding over the next couple of weeks to include games like Control Resonant, Marvel's Spider-Man 2, Arc Raiders, The Finals, No Man's Sky, and Hell Let Loose: Vietnam. While it's not quite as good as PSSR on the PS5 Pro, QSSR still does a noticeable job of adding detail and clarity without impacting performance. Sony added that since QSSR shares elements with PSSR, it makes games that support the PS5 Pro upscaling tech a "natural" fit for an upgrade on regular PS5 consoles. https://youtu.be/JYEQkLnlV7o Marvel's Spider-Man 2 is a good example, given Insomniac Games' familiarity with PSSR. The QSSR update is now available for the game, and Insomniac's head of technology, Mike Fitzgerald, said it'll apply to both Fidelity and Performance modes. For Control Resonant, Remedy Entertainment senior graphics programmer Erik Jansson said that QSSR will offer noticeable improvements in image stability and fine detail, and the update will be available in December. While there's no exact date for when Arc Raiders and The Finals will be updated, players can expect "increased sharpness, better environmental clarity and overall visual improvements," according to Embarl Studios technical art director Mikael Linderholm. Hello Games founder Sean Murray said that the No Man's Sky QSSR update will be out in a "few weeks" and will see the game look sharper on PS5 while maintaining "the best possible" frame rate. Finally, Paul Rustchynsky, game director at Expression Games, said that Hell Let Loose: Vietnam will also look cleaner and sharper on PS5 when the update is eventually available. If you're interested in seeing how different several of the games look with QSSR enabled, you can click the links below to see comparison videos: Control Resonant Arc Raiders No Man's Sky Hell Let Loose: Vietnam The PS5 turns six years old later this month, and as of November 10, it has surpassed 100 million consoles sold. Ordinarily, all eyes would be on the next PlayStation generation at this point-- which Sony says it is working on --and advances like QSSR may squeeze more life out of the PS5 before its successor arrives . Whatever form the next PlayStation takes, don't expect it to be cheap, as the current generation has gotten more expensive since 2020 and the PS6 could cost over $1,000 . Former PlayStation boss Shawn Layden recently touched on the topic, and he spoke about how true innovation from Sony would come in the form of cheaper hardware, not just better graphics.

title: Xbox Says Putting Ads In Games, Something No One Likes, Could Help Save Gaming
text: Xbox Cloud Gaming now has a free ad-supported version that's rolling out as part of Microsoft's bigger push to bring more ads to Xbox. Jonathan Stringfield, who worked on Activision's advertising push and is now doing some of the same work in his title as GM for Xbox Media Solutions, said in an interview that people shouldn't see this as a move by Xbox to cram ads into all of its games. “There is zero world where there is intention--written, explicit, implicit, or otherwise--that ads will be an option in all games. It might not even be the case on all features of the console, et cetera,” he told GamesBeat . “Where we want to have these integrated is places where it makes sense--where it can actually provide value in a positive way. Even if that means the total reach that we can have is going to be perhaps smaller than if we brute-forced it, that’s okay." Xbox now has more ads. Stringfield went on to point out how the gaming industry today is at a crossroads if the existing model is to survive. Many are saying it won't, or shouldn't, but Stringfield said if it does, then companies either need to "dramatically increase the price of games" or "find other mechanisms" that allow companies to make more money and keep the business healthy. Stringfield, whose job is to help sell ads, said ads could be a way forward. “When we talk about advertising--and things that are adjacent to it that amount to recurrent revenue, whether it’s subscriptions or otherwise--what this allows for is an alternative," he said. Xbox chief strategy officer, Matthew Ball, previously said Xbox's intention was not to "cram ads in everything." “Ads should be used to offer more affordable alternatives alongside today’s ad-free experiences, in the hopes more could play as a result. Similar to how Netflix and Disney+ have ad tiers with all the same content, but at half the price or so,” he said. “At no point do I even mention in-game ads. I personally believe interrupting the gameplay experience would be bad.” For Xbox Cloud Gaming, users can now stream their own games for free with ad-supported cloud gaming. Alternatively, people can purchase ad-free cloud playtime, or they can subscribe to Xbox Game Pass to get more time. However, starting this month, Xbox is putting hourly caps on how much people can stream before requiring them to pay more. The ads on Xbox Cloud Gaming come in the form of pre-roll ads that people watch before getting into a game; they don't interrupt gameplay, however. Video game prices have remained largely flat over the years, and this is part of the problem, some experts have said. Without price increases, the math just doesn't math when development costs and other expenses are factored in. For his part, Stringfield said price increases for games would not be "terribly popular," so he's looking at other systems, namely ads, to fill the gap. The biggest game of 2026, Rockstar's GTA 6 , costs $80 for its standard edition, scaling up to $100 for the Ultimate Edition and $400 for a collector's edition (which doesn't include the game) . For comparison, GTA 5 launched in 2013 at $60--that same $60 is worth about $86 today after inflation. This is why Take-Two CEO Strauss Zelnick believes GTA 6 is a true bargain --it's "cheaper" than GTA 5 was some 13 years ago, he says. But GTA 6 isn't the first game to charge $80--Nintendo ushered in this new era in 2025 with Mario Kart World. People like former PlayStation executive Shawn Layden have said for years that companies refusing to raise prices was actually detrimental and has caused numerous systemic problems , contributing to the situation the industry finds itself in. Layden said the price of new games ought to have gone up $10 for each new console generation, and when that didn’t happen, companies made efforts to extract more money from people with things like microtransactions, battle passes, and subscriptions. One Bank of America analyst believes the rest of the industry should follow Rockstar and start charging $80 for games . If more companies raise prices to $80 like Rockstar is doing with GTA 6, that doesn’t mean developers will stop hawking things like microtransactions, DLC, and battle passes. Instead, these efforts to increase ARPU will likely continue in concert with price hikes because why would a company cut off, or scale back, a revenue stream?

title: GTA 6 Passes 12 Million Copies Sold And $1.2 Billion In Revenue, And The Game Isn’t Even Out Yet
text: The video game research company Sensor Tower has updated its GTA 6 sales tracker to reveal the latest, albeit unofficial, sales data for the open-world crime game. According to Sensor Tower, GTA 6 has now sold 12.13 million total units via pre-purchases, which works out to about $1.18 billion in gross revenue. The report said PS5 sales are dominating the mix, with GTA 6 selling 9.08 million units on PS5 so far, compared to 3.06 million on Xbox Series X|S. That means of the 12.13 million GTA 6 sales so far, 75% are on PS5 and 25% on Xbox Series X|S. In total, GTA 6 sales for PS5 have so far reached $880 million in revenue, compared to $296 million for Xbox Series X|S. Sony and Microsoft keep about 30% of revenue due to their platform fees, so GTA 6 being a huge success directly benefits both of those companies. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=wmKu9Uow-os The huge gap in sales between platforms is not surprising because the PS5 is dominating Xbox Series X|S in terms of console sales. In fact, GTA 6 is breaking records on Xbox , Microsoft has said, and the sales numbers for GTA 6 on Xbox line up with Xbox's share of the console market . Sensor Tower is projecting as many as 25 million total pre-purchases for GTA 6 by launch , and if the 75/25 split holds, that would be about 18.5 million units on PS5 and 6.5 million on Xbox Series X|S. GTA 6 is the most preordered game of all time for PlayStation and Xbox . If the 10 million pre-purchase number is real, that would break a record for most preorders set by Cyberpunk 2077 (8 million) . Sony holds the marketing rights for GTA 6 on PS5, but that doesn't mean that Microsoft is doing nothing to try to promote the game. Just recently, Microsoft announced a GTA 6-inspired custom Xbox console that sits inside an alligator. Circana has released new data that shows that GTA 6 holds 29% purchase intent among US console and PC gamers. That means nearly 1 in 3 console and PC gamers in the US plan to buy GTA 6 –this is the highest purchase intent that Circana has ever measured for any game. GTA 6 may indeed be a gigantic hit commercially, and one that helps lift the entire industry with increased sales of hardware and accessories. But anyone looking to buy a new console to play GTA 6 is set for major sticker shock, as consoles today are more expensive than ever. Not only that, but GTA 6 is not going to save the industry’s many serious and deep-rooted issues, experts believe . GTA 6 launches on November 19 for PS5 and Xbox Series X|S. The game's file size is about 212GB , and thankfully, preloading is already underway . The game unlocks on November 19 at midnight local time , and that means US players will be among the last in the world to get in. title: The Xbox 25th Anniversary Console Restock Sold Out Before You Could Finish Reading This Headline
text: After quickly selling out earlier this year, Microsoft dropped a limited number of its 25th Anniversary Xbox Series X consoles for sale this week-- aaaaannnd they're already gone . Easily the best-looking Xbox Series X console thanks to its transparent green case, it looks like the majority of people looking to get one of these are out of luck, unless they're willing to pony up and pay extra for one of these consoles on sites like eBay, where they're currently being listed at next-gen console prices. Naturally, fans who missed out are livid, and online, they're calling out Xbox's first-come first-serve business model for selling the console, as opposed to a method like a lottery system that would even the playing field. Several disappointed buyers say that scalpers and bots go to all the remaining stock first, as they claim that it was sold out within seconds once again. People are especially mad at GameStop, as its dynamic pricing system had the console up for sale at the eye-watering price of $4,950, not including tax. https://twitter.com/AteThePrincess/status/2121107152362414300 Over on eBay, beggars can't be choosers, as people continue to pay an inflated price for this Xbox Series X. Sales of it are averaging around $2,500 per console, a significant mark-up from the $900 MSRP of the device. In comparison, both Nintendo and Sony have implemented lottery and queue-based reservation systems in the past, specifically designed to thwart scalpers and filter out automated bots. Last year for the rollout of the Switch 2 in Japan, Nintendo utilized an official lottery system via the My Nintendo Store, which saw over 2 million people enter. In western markets, Nintendo offered a direct invitation queue via regional Nintendo Accounts for verified active account holders. Sony's PS5 Pro has also become a hot item ahead of the launch of Grand Theft Auto 6, and recently, Sony instituted an anti-scalping lottery system via the official Sony Store in Japan. To qualify for the draw, entrants were required to have a Japanese PlayStation Network account and a verified history of at least 60 hours of playtime on a PS4 or PS5 across the preceding two years. But with Xbox hardware sales reaching historic lows recently ? Microsoft probably isn't too worried about who buys its consoles, so long as it sells them.

title: “You Guys Are F***ing Idiots”: Jeff Kaplan Takes Aim At Blizzard’s Overwatch 2 Reveal
text: Saying Overwatch 2 has had a rocky road since its 2019 reveal would be an understatement, and former Overwatch director Jeff Kaplan isn't a fan of how the game was first announced. Speaking to Gaming World Interviews , Kaplan didn't mince words about the BlizzCon 2019 opening ceremony, where Overwatch 2 was shown for the first time, as Blizzard promised numerous features it either walked back or didn't deliver. Kaplan said that from 2018 until his departure, he experienced constant friction with Blizzard's executive leadership over game direction, scheduling, and core game mechanics. This led him to confront leadership about the lack of a clear vision or business model for Overwatch 2, and to question the wisdom of announcing Overwatch 2 at the same time as Diablo 4. https://youtu.be/98HNSuXHtys "I got in a huge fight with, at the time, it wasn't Mike [Morhaime]. I loved Mike, who was the president of Blizzard, and another president of Blizzard, my executive producer, over announcing Overwatch 2. I went into their office, I’m like, 'What are we doing? We don’t really know what this game is; we don’t know what the business model is. This is a huge mistake.'" According to Kaplan, the new executives "had a lot to prove" when they joined Blizzard. "They wanted to prove that 'Blizzard's back and Blizzard still has it.' And I'm like, 'You guys are f***ing idiots,' you know? I don’t know how else to put it, but after three years of just getting worn down and not agreeing with any of the decisions that were being made on the franchise and not feeling like I had agency anymore--like before it used to be like I'm the game director I get to decide the direction the game goes. And starting in 2018, I lost that, and after three years of fighting for it back, I realized this company belongs to these corporate people now, the Blizzard executive team, the Activision team." Kaplan left Blizzard in 2021, saying Activision Blizzard’s financial arm told him that if Overwatch didn't meet certain financial goals, 1,000 people at the company would be laid off and the blame would fall on him. "The biggest f**k you moment I’ve had in my career--it felt surreal to be in that condition," Kaplan said earlier this year . These days, Kaplan is working on The Legend of California at the new studio he co-founded, Kintsugiyama. The Blizzard veteran recently spoke to GameSpot about the "humbling" reality of being an indie dev and more.

title: Fable Is Looking A Lot Darker Than We Expected
text: Amid a modest 25th-anniversary celebration , Xbox dropped a new preview of the Fable reboot. This snippet — which runs for under four minutes — offers plenty of gameplay and a closer look at some of the ghoulish enemies you'll face, set in a slice of Albion that looks surprisingly grim compared to the lighthearted Fable teasers that came before it. "The Hero of Briar Hill has entered the depths of Deepwood alongside Arden, a local Hero, to investigate why strange magical happenings have been troubling the people of Oakshire," the video synopsis reads. "Here, they cross a threshold where the natural magic of Deepwood appears corrupted by an outside force, and they discover hints as to who or what could be responsible." https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=iEZUY04k3eQ One thing to note about this snippet of gameplay is that it's pulled from the PC build of Fable, with the settings cranked up to Ultra. It's a pretty good-looking glimpse of what you can expect from Fable next year, even if it feels different from its cheekier predecessors and more like a feudal action slice reminiscent of Control Resonant toward the end, with its red-hued aesthetic. Of course, four minutes of Fable doesn't tell the whole story, and with the main campaign alone estimated to take 20 hours to finish , that doom-and-gloom feeling probably won't be present throughout the entire game. Fable launches February 23, 2027, for Xbox Series X|S, PS5, and PC, with Playground Games primarily handling development. Turn 10 Studios also assisted with development, and following recent changes at Xbox, it was merged into Playground Games. In addition to Fable, Xbox also revealed that new Wolfenstein and Doom games are in development, and Xbox CEO Asha Sharma’s open letter to the Xbox community suggested that future game development might be more reliant on AI .

title: Wolfenstein 3 Is Officially In Production At MachineGames
text: The long-rumored Wolfenstein 3 has been officially confirmed to be in development at MachineGames. The news follows many hints and rumors of a third game in MachineGames' planned Wolfenstein trilogy, the franchise's first new entry since Wolfenstein: Youngblood in 2019 and its first mainline title since 2017. Xbox CEO Asha Shar posted the announcement as part of Xbox's 25th anniversary celebrations, and Bethesda also shared the news in its own post. https://bsky.app/profile/bethesda.net/post/3n25q3afshc2v In a move borrowed from the film industry, the game announcement was accompanied by a look at Wolfenstein 3's script, showing that protagonist B.J. Blazkowicz is back and more fearsome than ever. Bethesda also shared a photo from a mocap session, confirming that actors Brian Bloom and Debra Wilson will return to reprise their roles as B.J. and Grace Walker, respectively. MachineGames has said that it always planned for a trilogy of Wolfenstein games featuring B.J., meaning Wolfenstein 3 will continue the story that started with The New Order in 2014. MachineGames, alongside Bethesda, has also released three Wolfenstein spin-offs: the prequel The Old Blood in 2015, 2019's Youngblood, which featured B.J.'s twin daughters as protagonists, and the VR experience Cyberpilot, also released in 2019. The studio took a break from the Wolfenstein franchise to develop 2024's critically acclaimed Indiana Jones and the Great Circle. We don't have any more details on Wolfenstein 3 at present, including a release window, but we'll likely hear more soon.

title: Candy Crush Is Celebrating Xbox’s 25th Anniversary With Halo, Fallout, And Doom Crossovers, Including Remixed Music
text: 2026 is the 25th anniversary of Xbox, and it's been a tough year for the brand with mass layoffs, studio closures/divestitures, and game cancellations. title: New Doom Game Seemingly Announced In The Weirdest Way After Half The Studio Was Laid Off
text: Xbox CEO Asha Sharma has announced that id Software is officially working on a new game, believed to be another Doom title. This is happening after Sharma oversaw id Software losing half of its staff to layoffs that were part of the Xbox "reset." Id Software replied to Sharma's post on Twitter to provide a few more details on the new game, which the team didn't say was a Doom game, but everyone suspects it will be. The studio said it's "incredibly excited" about the new game, which is in the works at id's studios in Texas and Frankfurt. Hugo Martin, an id Software veteran, is directing the game--don't expect to see or hear about it soon, though. "It'll be some time before we're ready to share more but we can't wait for you to see what we're working on," the developer said. A scene from Doom: The Dark Ages. Reporter Tom Warren said in July that id Software was in the "early stages" of developing a new Doom game, so this news today isn't totally surprising. Sharma cut staff at id Software (and numerous other Xbox studios around the world) earlier this year as part of a "reset" of the Xbox business. Marty Stratton of id Software recently said the studio is "doing great," despite the mass layoffs. Id Software's latest game was 2025's Doom: The Dark Ages. The game's newest update is coming on November 16, adding the new wave-based Slaughter mode .

title: Games Will Have A Physical Footprint Forever, Take-Two Boss Says, But It’ll Be “Very Small”
text: It's no secret that the market for physical video games is drying up, but don't expect physical media for gaming to go away entirely anytime soon, or ever, according to Take-Two's Strauss Zelnick. He told The Game Business that it "may not be the end" for physical media entirely in games, even with Sony killing off PlayStation discs in 2028 . He said there will "always be some physical business" for gaming, but it will be a "very small part of the business." Lucia and Jason in GTA 6. He likened the scale of it to the vinyl business for recorded music. Most people might stream music today, but the market for vinyl is still there--and it's growing. For Take-Two, however, Zelnick said its business today is 98% digital. Going all-digital has a lot of benefits for publishers, but it's mainly about making more money. For GTA 6, the most highly anticipated game release ever, Rockstar is not offering the game on a disc, but the game will appear in stores via a code-in-a-box version. GTA 6's $400 collector's edition comes with a range of physical goods (but not the game), and Rockstar is also releasing GTA 6's score on CD and vinyl , but the game itself remains a digital-only experience. GTA 6 launches on November 19 for PS5 and Xbox Series X|S. A PC edition and online multiplayer are both rumored to launch in 2027 .

title: This Happy Ending For Two Games With Identical Names Was A Headache For Nintendo
text: On November 25, two entirely separate games called Piece by Piece are releasing on Nintendo Switch. It's no coincidence, but the circumstances that led to this unusual situation certainly stem from a coincidence. Publisher No More Robots launched Piece by Piece, a cozy sim game full of cute animal characters, on Steam back in March. Two days later, studio Neon Polygons self-published an unrelated puzzle-platformer where you jump through literal puzzle pieces that you connect together--this game is also called Piece by Piece. What could have been a conflict between indie developers turned out to be the beginning of a wholesome business relationship. Both games were bundled together on Steam , and now No More Robots is publishing the Switch ports of both titles. https://bsky.app/profile/mikerose.bsky.social/post/3mzzqdmjqjs2m According to No More Robots co-founder Mike Rose, Neon Polygons "couldn't afford to bring their game to Switch," so No More Robots stepped in to publish the game for them. As with Steam, you can buy both games together in a bundle . It's undeniably a heartwarming and unique story, though one would assume that having to figure out the logistics behind launching two games that not only have the same name, but the same release date and publisher as well, was a nightmare on the backend of the Nintendo eShop. "And yes, Nintendo have ABSOLUTELY HATED THIS," Rose said in a social media post, adding that the publisher was questioned why it had two games with the same name "many, many times." At least the bundle doesn't also include the Pharrell Williams Lego movie Piece by Piece as well.

title: Disney Teases “Major Announcements” For The Game Awards
text: The Game Awards will air on Disney+ this year, and along with that, Disney has teased "major announcements and surprises" for its own games at the event. To be sure, The Game Awards will stream in other places, too, like YouTube and Twitch, so you won't need to sign up for Disney+ to watch. "As the evening unfolds, viewers can expect major announcements and surprises from some of Disney’s most anticipated titles in gaming," the company said . That's all that Disney had to say on the matter, but the tease has gotten people excited to theorize about the possibilities. For starters, Disney is already a big player in the world of video games, with nine different gaming franchises that have each generated at least $1 billion . One such franchise is Kingdom Hearts, and many are expecting news about Kingdom Hearts 4 soon. Beyond that, there are ongoing rumors about a new version of The Simpsons: Hit & Run . Another possibility is that Disney shares more about its partnership with Epic Games and Fortnite. “A number of launches coming up over the next two years … are going to demonstrate the value of this partnership,” Disney executive Dana Walder recently said. Disney could also share new details about its upcoming Star Wars gaming projects, including Star Wars Eclipse , or possibly the rumored Jedi 3 or Battlefront 3. Or Disney could show off some of its new Marvel projects, including the upcoming Iron Man game . Marvel's Blade also remains in development amid uncertainty about its developer, Arkane Lyon . Disney’s new CEO, Josh D’Amaro, is a big believer in games and has suggested gaming could be Disney’s next big growth-driver , after the company’s stock price has been flat over the past decade. Some have theorized that Disney could buy Epic and Fortnite to help grow the business, but nothing has materialized as of yet. The Game Awards are set for Thursday, December 10 from the Peacock Theater in Los Angeles. Keep checking back with GameSpot for more.

title: Xbox Has Spent 25 Years Tracking Your Gaming Habits; Now You Can See The Damage
text: It's the 25th anniversary of Xbox, and to celebrate, you can see how much time you've spent--or wasted, according to my parents--playing games on Xbox hardware over the years. Not to be confused with the end-of-year wrap-up that Xbox usually offers, Xbox Playback looks at your entire history, from when you first booted up a console to your current-day Achievements. It's a neat little celebratory feature, complete with a customized video and graphics that you can show off. In addition to the date you started playing on Xbox, it includes the first Xbox console you used, the first game you booted up, your total hours played, a breakdown of game genres, and more. (There are some limits on data during Xbox's early years, though.) You can try it out by signing in to your Xbox account through this link . I'm disgusted by the lack of Metal Gear Rising: Revengeance on my list. Other stats you can check out include the games you spent the most hours on, which ones you got a 100% Achievement rank in, and your longest streak of consecutive play days. Xbox says you can share your record online by scanning a QR code at the end of the video that plays--just in case you want to share how many hours you've sunk into Viva Piñata over the decades. While this is a fun way to look back at your Xbox history, it does come at a bittersweet time for Microsoft's gaming brand. This year has been brutal for Xbox employees amid a grand "reset" spearheaded by Xbox CEO Asha Sharma, as scores of jobs have been lost and several game studios have left the company. Xbox is now focused on chasing big hits across PC, consoles, and mobile, with an ambitious goal of becoming more profitable than its biggest gaming rivals, Sony and Nintendo, by 2030. Sharma has also written about what the next 25 years for Xbox could look like, with her open letter suggesting that artificial intelligence will play a greater role in the future of video game development.

title: Final Fantasy 14 Players Are Mourning The Loss Of The Game’s Legendary Bassist
text: The Final Fantasy 14 community is in mourning following news that Eikichi Iwai, the bassist for the game's house band, The Primals, has died at the age of 57, and is taking to the MMORPG's main hub cities to honor his legacy. An "Important Announcement" post on the official FF14 website from developer Square Enix on November 11 broke the news, and stated the development team was "deeply saddened" to inform the community of Iwai's passing. "Having witnessed his truly unforgettable performance on stage at the recent Final Fantasy 14 Fan Festival in Japan, the sudden news of his passing has come as a profound shock," the statement reads. "The members of The Primals and the entire FF14 development and operations team are overcome with deep sorrow. "As we reflect on all that Eikichi-san has left behind, our thoughts are with him, and we offer our heartfelt condolences." The Primals, with Eikichi Iwai second from the left. The Primals, composed of Iwai on bass, composer Masayoshi Soken, localization lead Michael-Christopher Koji Fox, and band members Tetsuya Tachibana and GUNN, are behind some of FF14's most memorable tracks. Iwai's bass in particular stands out on songs like Shadowbringers' To the Edge and Stormblood's Amatsu Kaze . The band performed worldwide at various FF14 Fan Festivals, as well as at a UK rock festival , earlier this year. https://www.reddit.com/r/ffxiv/comments/1xtygrg/rest_in_peace_eikichi_iwai_vigil_in_siren_limsa/ Final Fantasy 14's community has a reputation as being one of the best, and most welcoming, in gaming, so it's no surprise it took the time to honor Iwai's passing. As spotted on Reddit , the game's playerbase has come together to pay their respects Iwai, with large gatherings of players holding firelight vigils in his memory across the game's various servers and cities. https://www.reddit.com/r/ffxiv/comments/1xtgw3a/memorial_to_eikichi_iwai_on_omega_chaos_rest_in/ "It's so good to see everyone come together, he deserves it for playing such a big role in the music we've fallen in love with. May he rest peacefully," one community member wrote . More of Iwai and The Primals' music will be heard in Final Fantasy 14's next upcoming expansion, Evercold, set to release on February 23, 2027.

title: Xbox CEO’s 25th Anniversary Message Is About AI, Even If She Won’t Say It
text: As Xbox celebrates its 25th anniversary, Xbox CEO Asha Sharma has shared her thoughts on where gaming is going over the next 25 years, and people are saying her message is really more about pushing AI. Sharma said modern games demonstrate the "heights of human craft in ways unimaginable just decades ago." However, the costs, resources, and risks that companies need to take on have "grown just as dramatically," she said. "As a result, too many ideas never become games, and too many games fall short of what their creators imagined. For decades, this has been the unavoidable tradeoff of ambition. We must change this," she said. The 25th anniversary of Xbox has been rough for the company. Historically, to create anything at scale required immense resources, but Sharma said that's changing. Without saying AI, Sharma said it won't be long until a single person can "wield capabilities that once required entire nations." "A small team will be able to build worlds that today demand hundreds of developers and hundreds of millions of dollars. And our largest studios will be able to pursue ambitions as far beyond today’s games as Microsoft Flight Simulator 2024 is from its first entry in 1982," she said. Sharma went on to say that the future of gaming "will look more like its beginning," which is to say that a small team with a bold idea can make a real impact. "Our responsibility is to deliver great games, unmistakable hardware, and give more people the chance to make something the world has never seen," she said. Xbox recently launched Xbox Labs, which is a pretty obvious push into the world of vibe-coded games . Sharma has promised that she has "no tolerance for bad AI." She added, “We will not chase short-term efficiency or flood our ecosystem with soulless AI slop.” Sharma became Xbox CEO earlier this year, replacing Phil Spencer. Sharma immediately made lots of big changes to "reset" the business, including mass layoffs, game cancellations, and studio closures/divestitures. Sharma comes from an AI background, having previously been an executive on the CoreAI team at Microsoft. She may be bullish about having smaller teams make big games going forward, but it's not an all-or-nothing approach. After all, Xbox continues to own and fund large-scale, expensive productions like Call of Duty, World of Warcraft, and Forza just to name a few. AI is a big push for Xbox's owner, Microsoft, so it makes sense to see Sharma undertake efforts to increase Xbox's own efforts in that department. This is happening after a study of game developers found that more developers than ever think generative AI is bad for gaming.

title: Mario Kart World Switch 2 Bundle Black Friday Deal Brings The Price Back To 2025 Levels
text: Nintendo has announced its 2026 Black Friday deals, with a Mario Kart World Switch 2 hardware bundle as the centerpiece for $500. The Switch 2 launched in 2025 with a similar bundle for the same price, but it was discontinued at the end of the year. It later returned , but at a higher price point--$550. Now, the bundle is on "sale" again, though it's the same price as it was in 2025 before the price hikes. In addition to a digital copy of the game and the console, it comes with a three-month Nintendo Switch Online membership. The Mario Kart World Switch 2 bundle is back to its 2025 price. The bundle goes on sale November 22 and will be available through December 5. It's not the only hardware bundle that people can buy, as Nintendo also offers a system with a digital copy of Nintendo Switch Sports Resort and three months of Switch Online for $530. This bundle is not on sale for Black Friday, though. Get the Mario Kart World Switch 2 hardware bundle here: Amazon Best Buy Walmart Target Additionally, for just one week--November 22-29--Nintendo will offer games like Donkey Kong Bananza and Super Mario Galaxy + Super Mario Galaxy 2 for $20 off. What's more, Nintendo announced that the Nintendo eShop and the Nintendo Store will offer a range of deals November 19-December 2, but it hasn’t yet detailed what you can expect. Black Friday used to be just one day of deals--the day after Thanksgiving in the US--but now it's an entire season of savings. Keep checking back with GameSpot for more Black Friday deals in the days ahead.

title: GTA 6’s Jason Can Live His Best Life By Drinking A Beer And Eating A Donut Simultaneously
text: Rockstar's Grand Theft Auto 6 looks like it will have an impressive attention to detail, and that includes how one of the main characters, Jason, can drink a beer and eat a donut at the same time. Now that's living. Rockstar boss Rob Nelson geeked out to The Guardian about GTA 6's finer details, including this one. According to the report, Jason can "take bites of a donut with one hand while sipping a beer with the other." Drink up. It’s unclear whether this is under the player’s active control or it just happens. In any event, the report also mentioned how Rockstar paid close attention to "the way that Jason eats a hot dog." These are very important details. GTA 6 features a body-shaping system, so if Jason, or Lucia, drink a lot of beer and pound hot dogs and donuts, they'll likely gain weight. But that weight can then be transformed into muscle by hitting the gym and pumping out sets . Another example of Rockstar's attention to detail in GTA 6 is how Jason can buy a six-pack of beer, then start jogging, holding the beers in the crook of his arm. The game shows you the liquid sloshing around in the bottles as he runs. GTA 6's attention to detail is a little ridiculous , with Rockstar seemingly going all out to create little details that players may never even notice . GTA 6 launches on November 19 for PS5 and Xbox Series X|S. Preloading is underway now, but the game itself doesn't unlock until November 19 at midnight local time.

title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang Resigns, Effective Immediately
text: Nvidia has announced that Jensen Huang has resigned as president and CEO of the company, effective immediately. Nvidia's current Chief Financial Officer, Colette Kress, will serve as interim CEO while keeping her CFO duties until a permanent replacement for Huang can be found. Harvey C. Jones, a longtime tech executive and investor, has been appointed as Nvidia's first-ever Chair of the Board, and the company says that operations, product plans, and customer commitments will continue without interruption. Nvidia's Q3 2017 financial results will still be reported on its scheduled date of November 17. Things began to look dire for Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang after it was revealed that he'd been involved in an extramarital affair with a suspected Chinese spy. This week, news broke that he'd also taken part in a second affair with one of his executives. According to The New York Times , the Nvidia board of directors scheduled a meeting to discuss the situation, just days after launching an independent investigation into him. After the affair was first exposed, Nvidia quickly issued a statement saying that none of the company's secrets, or US state secrets, had been compromised. Huang also issued a letter to Nvidia employees, apologizing to his wife and children. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang With AI technology taking off in the last couple of years, Nvidia has become a major supplier of the crucial hardware components powering this boom. While the company is best known for its graphics cards, its fortunes have risen exponentially as it has focused more heavily on AI chips, with Huang becoming the face of the AI boom in the US. Huang is also Nvidia's founder, having started the company in 1993 and run its day-to-day operations for decades. With a 3.56% stake, he's also Nvidia's largest shareholder. His removal could have huge ramifications for the company, given how involved he was in running it and the reported lack of a succession plan . The revelation of a second affair has seen Nvidia's stock tumble, and the company's board may feel pressured to remove him as CEO to do some damage control. "If Jensen Huang is ousted as is expected, an already challenging environment for Nvidia investors and employees will become considerably more difficult," chief market strategist at JonesTrading Mike O’Rourke told CNN . "Nvidia is currently the most important company in the world. "The new CEO will need to make an extensive appraisal of the company, and Jensen’s successor will not have the same latitude or deference to pursue circular deals and pursue aggressive sales tactics."

title: Intergalactic: The Heretic Prophet Has Some Unexpected Anime Influences
text: After years of post-apocalyptic survival stories and archaeological adventures, Intergalactic: The Heretic Prophet looks like a fresh opportunity for Naughty Dog to showcase a new sci-fi universe. Visually, the game draws on '80s sci-fi movies with analog technology and ancient hardware like CD players, but you can also thank a genre-defining anime film for shaping Intergalactic's look and feel. In an interview with Patton Oswalt during the Comic Creators Block Party 2026, Naughty Dog director Neil Druckmann said that Akira inspired Intergalactic on multiple levels, alongside other big anime properties like Cowboy Bebop . "For Intergalactic, we actually took a lot of inspiration from anime. Akira--everybody loves Akira--just like the animation, the big ideas, the kind of philosophical sci-fi ideas within that," Druckmann said. "We took a lot of inspiration from anime, stylistic inspiration, how they approach the story. The big kind of philosophical questions and ideas. We really want to tackle that, and surprise players in interesting ways. By the time you get to the end of Akira, it just goes on this wild ride. And we want to take someone on a similar wild ride." https://twitter.com/IntergalacticES/status/2120653537847742808 Druckmann mentioned that he grew up with the laser-disc version of Akira, the landmark 1988 anime film directed by Katsuhiro Otomo. It's not hard to see that influence visually, as the protagonist Jordan A. Mun wears a jacket that looks like it was pilfered from the wardrobe of Akira lead Shotaro Kaneda, and her spaceship also looks like it was manufactured by the same company responsible for the hotheaded biker's iconic motorcycle--maybe we'll even see an Akira slide in the game. Philosophically, Akira covers a wide range of topics explored over the decades, with the film primarily centered on themes of human technological overreach, spiritual immaturity, and the cyclical nature of creation and destruction. Those ideas have been debated for decades, and Naughty Dog has proven adept at balancing heavy themes with engaging gameplay, particularly in The Last of Us, which balanced a tale of vengeance with shootouts and stealth. A closer look at its themes isn't too far off either, as Druckmann confirmed that Naughty Dog will have more to share about the game in 2027 .

title: Intergalactic: The Heretic Prophet Is Entering Its Final Stage Of Development, With More To Come In 2027
text: Intergalactic: The Heretic Prophet developer Naughty Dog has been largely radio silent about its upcoming sci-fi game since it was first revealed in 2024, but it looks like 2027 will bring a lot more information. Speaking to Patton Oswalt during the Comic Creators Block Party 2026, director Neil Druckmann teased that the game is entering its "final stage" of production. "We've only teased it, so I can't talk too much about it," Druckmann said. "But we're kind of like at the last stages of production, where we can play it, and we're refining and polishing it, and I can't wait to show it to the world." https://twitter.com/IntergalacticES/status/2120653537847742808 Druckmann also said that after 20 years of relatively grounded games set on Earth, Intergalactic represented an opportunity for the studio to combine everything it learned from its biggest franchises into an experience that blends "cinematic" storytelling with deep gameplay. "Something we've been really hungry for is to go sci-fi. We used to have another game franchise, called Jak and Daxter. We wanted to take everything we learned from that franchise--which is sci-fi, fantasy, the kind of pulp-action adventure stuff we learned with Uncharted, the kind of serious drama we got from The Last of Us. It really is a combination of those three franchises, and we really wanted to expand our deep gameplay systems. Like, can we sustain the kind of cinematic storytelling we're used to doing, and go even deeper with gameplay systems?" So when will we actually get to see the game in action? "We're going to show a lot next year, Druckman said. "We're going to show gameplay, more of the story. I think we’re going to really surprise people with what they think the game is and what it actually is." Previously, reports said Naughty Dog has entered a period of crunch to get the game over the finish line. Focused on the protagonist Jordan A. Mun-- played by Tati Gabrielle --a bounty hunter who becomes stranded on a planet called Sempiria, this will be Naughty Dog's first new IP after two decades of Uncharted and The Last of Us games, as well as its first original PS5 release. In addition to Intergalactic, Naughty Dog is reportedly also working on The Last of Us: Part 3 .

title: Marvel 1943: Rise Of Hydra Isn’t Canceled, But Don’t Get Too Excited
text: Amid multiple delays and radio silence, a rumor that Marvel 1943: Rise of Hydra had been canceled began circulating this week. Developer Skydance quickly said the game is on track and nearly done—but it might not be what you expect. According to Kotaku , executive producer Lu Gigliotti told Skydance employees that he had spoken with the studio's executive leadership team, and that the game had not been canceled. "They asked me to make sure you all hear that directly. There is no truth to these claims," Giglotti reportedly wrote in the Skydance Slack group. Kotaku added that the game is approaching its Alpha milestone and is "close to done," but after reportedly running significantly over budget, the vision for this project has been scaled back. Marvel 1943 was also originally envisioned as a Netflix game before it was announced for PC and consoles, but most of its action is apparently mapped to a single button, and it's "lacking significant interaction" during gameplay. https://youtu.be/_T0j_rKZhT0 Essentially, the game might be structurally similar to Quantic Dream's interactive stories like Detroit: Become Human, rather than a meaty brawler like Insomniac's Spider-Man games. "We're continuing development on it, but Amy and the team have big ambitions for the level of quality that they want to hit. They are a relatively small team considering the AAA quality that they're delivering,” senior executive Shawn Kittelsen said earlier this year about the game's lengthy development. "What you've seen in previous footage is what the game looks like, and we're making it with a fraction of the resources that you see on other AAA games of the same type, and really trying to push a new development model that's a lot more responsible and sustainable." First announced in 2022 and fully revealed in 2024, Marvel 1943: Rise of Hydra drew attention for its good-looking graphics and a storyline featuring multiple characters, including Captain America and Black Panther. The new report comes in the wake of layoffs at Skydance's parent group, Paramount Games Studio , which is also changing following Paramount's acquisition of Warner Bros. While live-service Marvel games like Marvel Rivals and Marvel Snap continue to draw in players, the same can't be said for the big-budget Wolverine game that was released earlier this year. Despite a strong start in September, the game quickly lost momentum and has sold 2.4 million units so far.

title: Steam’s Growing Review Backlog Has Cost Another Game Its Launch Date
text: Steam's growing backlog for approving game builds appears to be getting worse, as yet another studio's game is stuck in the purgatory of the platform's review program. Australia Did It: End-of-the-World Railway Defense Business , a post-apocalyptic game about keeping a cargo railway running after society has collapsed, was originally scheduled to launch on November 10, but it's stuck waiting for Steam's mandatory QA review before it can be published. "Unfortunately, we're stuck waiting for Steam to review and approve our launch build. We have been waiting for a few weeks now and sadly don't know when they will finally get around to it," Australia Did It publisher Mystic Forge wrote in an update. "We're hoping to be able to launch as soon as possible and will update all of you the second we get an update. We really appreciate all of your continued support and apologize for the situation. We can't wait for you to check out the final game and hope to be able to get it into your hands soon!" https://youtu.be/pX7HVir6l2o Australia Did It co-developer and game designer Rami Ismail said the game was originally submitted on October 20, and a minor controller issue caused it to fail. That bug was fixed the same day, but since then, Ismail and Aesthecian Labs have been stuck waiting for Steam approval. "We've been in the queue again ever since, and have followed up with Valve several times to no result," Rami explained in an email to GameSpot. "The issue was that our in-game feedback functionality does not allow you to send feedback--from a keyboard text input--via controller. I'm used to this kind of hold-and-wait pattern on console, but not really on Steam. 10-14 days pre-launch is usually enough to fail twice over, and usually you only get failed on serious issues." With reviews for Australia Did It already out, and the game on plenty of wishlists, not having it ready for its scheduled launch isn't doing it any favors. "Pre-emptively delaying the launch would've hurt, as did not doing so," Ismail added. "We decided to take that gamble and trust in Valve's willingness to come through for developers - it seems we bet wrong." Is a deluge of AI slop to blame for Australia Did It being stuck in QA limbo? Ismail explained that Steam can set its own policies and host "slopware" games on its own servers, but it's also having a negative effect on developers. "At 30% off of every game sold on the platform, I have to admit I don't really care what the reason is. It's likely slopware is a part of the issue, but the fact that slopware can exist on Steam is their own policy. Whatever the situation, Steam losing the agility and access for developers to launch with minimal friction will mean developers have to treat it more like a console - which means we have to be more careful about launches." While releasing the game on another platform like the Epic Games Store could be one solution, Ismail noted that the "commercial potential" is much lower than on Steam, which accounts for the lion's share of PC game sales. "With Epic, we're just trading the one billionaire for the other, and the commercial potential is also much lower. For now we're stuck with Steam for commercial game releases." Ordinarily, every game submitted to Steam undergoes a series of checks to ensure that it'll work on the launcher, a process that used to take a few days. Lately, multiple developers have been complaining that this process now takes up to two weeks, and in some instances, longer, as Steam is reportedly battling to work through a backlog of submitted games. Several studios have blamed a flood of AI slop games, which regularly fail QA and are then resubmitted for review, gumming up the works and creating a bottleneck. Recently, Valve introduced new measures to help speed up the process, but it's unclear if they've had any real impact. Under the new guidelines, games submitted for QA are required to be run through the Steam launcher for a minimum of five minutes; there will be stricter enforcement on images so that players aren't misled; Steam will run automated checks to flag broken or incomplete achievements; and advertised features will need to be included.
